blocks.content: No insider shall communicate, provide, or allow access to any unpublished price sensitive information relating to a company or securities.

rows: Directly associated with the company through directorship, employment, or fiduciary relation
Presumed to be connected due to personal or organizational proximity to a connected person
Directors, Key Managerial Personnel (KMPs), Officers, and Employees
Immediate relatives, firm partners, holding/subsidiary company officials
On SEBI to prove that the individual possessed UPSI during trading
On the individual to prove non-possession of UPSI

items: Trading window closure is mandatory from the end of every quarter until 48 hours after financial results are made public.
For 'deemed connected persons', the burden of proof shifts to the individual to show they were not in possession of UPSI.
Contra-trades executed within a period of 6 months from a previous trade attract strict disciplinary and financial penalties.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Insider trading refers to dealing in securities while in possession of Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI).
SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 provide the legal framework to prevent market abuse in India.
A Connected Person includes any individual associated with the company who has access to UPSI through employment, contractual, or fiduciary relationships.
Compliance Officers in listed entities are responsible for setting trading window closures and pre-clearing trades of designated persons.
Communication or procurement of UPSI is illegal except for legitimate purposes, performance of duties, or discharge of legal obligations.
